newsitem.title: LATVIA: MPS TO SCRUTINISE SECURITIES WATCHDOG BOARD.
newsitem.headline: MPS TO SCRUTINISE SECURITIES WATCHDOG BOARD.

text.p: Candidates for the remaining three securities board posts will be scrutinised by the political factions' co-operation body before the parliament budget committee passes its decision on Wednesday, politicians said.
The Democratic party Saimnieks insisted on Tuesday that MPs make their views known on the candidates before a budget committee decision is passed, politicians said.

The new candidates suggested by Viktors Gustsons, the chairman of the commission, include Andris Miglavs, acting manager of the State Agrarian Policy Institute, and Pauls Dzintars Kalninsh, co-owner of the U.S. based consultancy Baltic Ventures Inc.
The third is Janis Brazovskis, currently deputy head of the central bank's department of credit institution supervision.
The securities commission is a state body which supervises the financial markets.
It had four of its planned seven board members approved by parliament earlier this month, making it capable of decision making.
